stories.headline: 2026 Ballon d'Or: Full men's, women's short lists, host city change, more
stories.summary: The 2026 Ballon d'Or short lists are out. Here's who could win the biggest individual prizes in men's and women's soccer.
stories.body:
It's nearly that time again.

The 2026 Ballon d'Or awards -- the annual ceremony in which France Football Magazine crowns the best men's and women's players in the world -- are fast approaching, with the short list for each award announced on Tuesday.

The Ballon d'Or trophies are handed out based on the criteria of: "1) Individual performances, decisive and impressive character, 2) Team performances and achievements, 3) Class and fair play."

Any player in world football is eligible, no matter the league they play in or their country of origin, and the short lists are decided by a jury of 100 journalists from around the world. So who is nominated for this year's awards, and who could win?

When is the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony, and why isn't it in Paris?

The 2026 Ballon d'Or awards, which have long been presented by France Football Magazine, will be handed out on Oct. 26. There will be a difference this year, though: The star-studded ceremony will not take place in Paris. Instead, it will be held in London at The London Palladium theater to mark the gala's 70th anniversary.

The first Ballon d'Or ceremony was a much more humble affair, held in Blackpool, England, and awarded to 41-year-old star forward Stanley Matthews.

Matthews was an all-time England great who spent the majority of his career at Blackpool and Stoke City and, when announcing the venue change, was described by organizers as a "true ambassador of football."

"As the Ballon d'Or becomes of septuagenarian age, it is fitting in such a landmark year to celebrate the finest present-day exponents of the beautiful game in the beating heart of the country that first conceived of it," organizers added.

Full 30-player Ballon d'Or short list

Jude Bellingham
Club: Real Madrid

Country: England

Bellingham didn't win a trophy with Real Madrid for the second year running, but the all-action midfielder was an important pillar of England's bronze medal-winning display at the 2026 World Cup. The 23-year-old scored seven goals at the tournament and his virtuoso two-goal display against Mexico in the round of 16 is likely to go down in Three Lions' folklore.

Pau Cubarsí
Club: Barcelona

Country: Spain

A debut nomination for 19-year-old center back Cubarsi, who played an important role in Barcelona's 2025-26 title win before being crowned Best Young Player at the World Cup after playing every single minute of Spain's monumental victory, keeping seven clean sheets along the way. He is also nominated for the Kopa Trophy, which is awarded to the best player aged 21 or younger.

Marc Cucurella
Club: Chelsea / Real Madrid

Country: Spain

Cucurella was a mainstay for Chelsea in the Premier League in 2025-26 before completing a transfer to Real Madrid during the World Cup. The energetic left back played every single minute for Spain at the tournament, and even provided two assists before ending his summer as a world champion.

Ousmane Dembélé
Club: Paris Saint-Germain

Country: France

Dembélé won the 2025 Ballon d'Or after starring for Paris Saint-Germain in the first of their back-to-back Champions League wins in 2024-25. Having repeated the feat with the club last season, the 29-year-old winger also accrued six goals and two assists for France at the 2026 World Cup.

Luis Díaz
Club: Bayern Munich

Country: Colombia

Diaz was part of a Bayern Munich team that amassed 122 league goals in just 34 Bundesliga matches last season, with the Colombia forward accounting for 15 of them. He then scored one goal and notched an assist as his country were jettisoned from the World Cup at the round-of-16 stage on penalties by Switzerland.

Bruno Fernandes
Club: Manchester United

Country: Portugal

One of the most reliable creative forces in the Premier League, Fernandes scored nine goals and weighed in with 21 assists for Manchester United in 2025-26, thus breaking the league's single-season assist record in the process. It then came as little surprise to see the Portuguese maestro crowned Premier League Player of the Season.

Erling Haaland
Club: Manchester City

Country: Norway

Despite suffering an extended fallow period during the second half of the 2025-26 Premier League campaign that saw him notch just three league goals between January and mid-April, Haaland still powered to a third Golden Boot with 27 goals in 35 games. The Norway striker then scored seven goals in his debut World Cup outing while becoming one of the most popular personalities at the tournament.

Gabriel Magalhães
Club: Arsenal

Country: Brazil

Gabriel kept 17 clean sheets for Arsenal in their title-winning 2025-26 season, helping to solidify one of the most effective defensive lines in world football.

Harry Kane
Club: Bayern Munich

Country: England

One of the favorites to lift the 2026 Ballon d'Or, Kane scored an astounding 67 goals in 58 games for Bayern Munich last season across all competitions, including 36 goals in 31 Bundesliga games. However, the prolific striker did fall short in his quest to win both the Champions League and the World Cup -- though he did technically captain England to a third-place finish at the latter.

Achraf Hakimi
Club: Paris Saint-Germain

Country: Morocco

Hakimi made only 18 appearances for PSG in the league last season but still ended up as a title and Champions League winner with the French giants. The right back also won the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations with Morocco -- although they lost the final to Senegal, the result was overturned by organizers due to their opponents prematurely leaving the pitch -- and he reached the quarterfinals of the World Cup the following summer.

Lamine Yamal
Club: Barcelona

Country: Spain

Yamal scored 24 goals in 45 games for Barcelona in all competitions as the Catalans wrapped up the Spanish league title in 2025-26. A lingering hamstring injury forced the winger to sit out the very start of the World Cup as he managed his fitness, but he was able to feature in the group stage in a reduced capacity. He then gradually grew in stature as the tournament progressed, with Spain ultimately emerging victorious.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia
Club: Paris Saint-Germain

Country: Georgia

Instrumental for Paris Saint-Germain in their second successive Champions League victory, the Georgia winger relished playing on the big European stage and registered a sequence of 10 goals and six assists along the way.

Marquinhos
Club: Paris Saint-Germain

Country: Brazil

Rock-solid at the heart of the Paris Saint-Germain defense, 32-year-old center back Marquinhos split his 32 appearances equally between Ligue 1 and the Champions League in 2025-26, and ended up winning both.

Sadio Mané
Club: Al Nassr

Country: Senegal

A fifth career nomination for veteran forward Mane, who pitched in with 14 goals in 36 games for Al Nassr last season as they were crowned champions of the Saudi Pro League. The 34-year-old Senegal star also guided his side to the final of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations.

Lautaro Martínez
Club: Inter Milan

Country: Argentina

Martinez won the Serie A and Coppa Italia double with Inter Milan in 2025-26, finishing as top goal scorer in the former and being crowned the best striker in the league as a result. He also scored three goals in eight games to help Argentina reach the final of the 2026 World Cup.

Kylian Mbappé
Club: Real Madrid

Country: France

He may have gone two seasons without winning anything with Real Madrid, but Mbappe hasn't been shy in putting himself forward for the 2026 Ballon d'Or, remarking that this year would be a "good year" for him to win it. The striker scored 42 goals in 44 games for Madrid and duly carried his fine form into the World Cup with France, where he claimed the Golden Boot with an impressive 10 goals to his name.

Nuno Mendes
Club: Paris Saint-Germain

Country: Portugal

A league and European double winner with Paris Saint-Germain with the Portugal international routinely proving to be among the very best left backs in the world.

Lionel Messi
Club: Inter Miami

Country: Argentina

With a record-extending 17th Ballon d'Or nomination, Messi is once again in the running to claim what would be a ninth career Ballon d'Or at the grand age of 39. The superstar is still scoring and assisting freely with Inter Miami in MLS, but his inspirational performances -- encompassing eight goals and four assists in eight games -- for Argentina at the World Cup this summer saw him come close to captaining his country to a second successive World Cup triumph, only for the dream to fall apart against Spain in the final.

Michael Olise
Club: Bayern Munich

Country: France

Nominated last year but finishing 30th out of 30 in the polling, Olise has seen his stock rise immeasurably over the past 12 months. The stylish, skillful attacking midfielder was an intrinsic part of the Bayern Munich side that cantered to the 2025-26 Bundesliga title and while he may not have found the net for France during their run to the World Cup semifinals this summer, Olise did lay on seven assists -- three more than any other player.

João Neves
Club: Paris Saint-Germain

Country: Portugal

He may only be 21 years old, but Neves has already developed into one of the most coveted midfielders in world football. A metronomic presence in the middle for Paris Saint-Germain and a Ligue 1 and Champions League double winner last time out.

Willian Pacho
Club: Paris Saint-Germain

Country: Ecuador

Highly rated Ecuador center back Pacho made 44 appearances for Paris Saint-Germain last season, winning the league and European double.

Julián Quiñones
Club: Al Qadsiah

Country: Mexico

Quiñones outscored Ivan Toney and Cristiano Ronaldo in the Saudi Pro League with his club Al Qadsiah, bagging 33 goals to top the chart in 2025-26 before scoring four goals for Mexico at the 2026 World Cup.

Declan Rice
Club: Arsenal

Country: England

One of the most dependable and versatile midfielders in world football, Rice was a Premier League title winner with Arsenal in 2025-26, with five goals and 11 assists thrown in for good measure. He also started all seven of England's games at the World Cup, even scoring in the topsy-turvy bronze medal tie against France.

Rodri
Club: Manchester City / Barcelona

Country: Spain

The 2024 Ballon d'Or winner endured a fairly underwhelming 2025-26 season at club level with Manchester City though he did seem to recapture his form just in time for the World Cup, where he pulled the strings in magisterial fashion for Spain on their way to lifting the trophy before wrapping up a £65million transfer to Barcelona in the aftermath.

Fabián Ruiz
Club: Paris Saint-Germain

Country: Spain

After an incredible season with Paris Saint-Germain and Spain, Ruiz can now claim to have won it all by adding a World Cup winners' medal to an enviable collection that already included the European Championship, the UEFA Nations League, the Champions League, various league titles and a host of other major honors.

Ferran Torres
Club: Barcelona / Paris Saint-Germain

Country: Spain

Torres scored 21 goals in 49 games for Barcelona in their title-winning 2025-26 campaign, though his crowning glory must surely be scoring the goal that saw Spain pip Argentina to win the 2026 World Cup. He left Barcelona this summer to join PSG.

William Saliba
Club: Arsenal

Country: France

Alongside defensive partner Gabriel, Saliba formed a watertight barrier at the back as Arsenal cut and thrust their way to the 2025-26 Premier League title.

Dayot Upamecano
Club: Bayern Munich

Country: France

Upamecano won the 2025-26 German title with Bayern Munich and was named in the Bundesliga team of the year thereafter, despite only making 24 appearances. He then played eight times for France at the 2026 World Cup, conceding just two goals before Spain knocked them out at the semifinal stage.

Vinícius Júnior
Club: Real Madrid

Country: Brazil

Vinicius Junior scored 22 goals in 53 games for Real Madrid last season, but frustratingly ended the campaign with little to show for his attacking endeavors. He then contributed four goals and an assist for Brazil at the World Cup.

Vitinha
Club: Paris Saint-Germain

Country: Portugal

Another of Paris Saint-Germain's double winners, Vitinha made 50 appearances and scored seven goals for the French giants over the course of the 2025-26 season while being named in both the official Ligue 1 and Champions League teams of the season.

Full 30-player Ballon d'Or Féminin short list

Selma Bacha
Club: OL Lyonnes

Country: France

As one of the leading left backs in the game, Bacha helped Lyonnes to a domestic treble and another Champions League final, adding 13 assists to help maintain OL Lyonnes' dominance.

Barbra Banda
Club: Orlando Pride

Country: Zambia

With 14 goals in 21 games, Banda has not slowed down her ruthlessness in front of goal, making her one of the most prominent attackers in the world.

Klara Bühl
Club: Bayern Munich

Country: Germany

Even though she registered 10 goals for Bayern Munich this season, it is her 23 assists across 37 matches that have made Bühl a worthy nominee, leading the German champions to a domestic treble.

Esmee Brugts
Club: Barcelona

Country: Netherlands

In her first nomination for the Ballon d'Or, Brugts registered 13 goals and 11 assists across 48 matches for Barcelona highly contributing to another quadruple-winning campaign.

Mariona Caldentey
Club: Arsenal

Country: Spain

Caldentey helped guide Arsenal to the inaugural Champions Cup title and retained Spain's Nations League trophy with her meticulous work rate and control in the midfield.

Scarlett Camberos
Club: Club América

Country: Mexico

As the first female Mexican player to be nominated for the Ballon d'Or, Camberos has already made history. She scored 27 goals and registered seven assists when leading Club América to win the Concacaf Women's Champions Cup.

Kerstin Casparij
Club: Manchester City

Country: Netherlands

The Dutch defender started almost all of City's victorious Women's Super League campaign, captaining the side when needed, adding seven assists and helping the team to another FA Cup victory.

Temwa Chawinga
Club: Kansas City Current

Country: Malawi

Chawinga's impressive 15-goal tally played a key role in leading the Kansas City Current to the NWSL Shield, highlighting her crucial contribution to the team's outstanding regular-season campaign.

Cata Coll
Club: Barcelona

Country: Spain

Keeping 23 clean sheets in total, Coll ensured Barcelona claimed another quadruple and even kept a clean sheet during the Champions League final. She only conceded 18 goals all season in 39 games.

Melchie Dumornay
Club: OL Lyonnes

Country: Haiti

Leading Lyonnes' attack, Dumornay netted 21 goals in the 2025-26 season, winning Première Ligue Player of the Year and guiding Lyonnes to another Champions League final. She added 12 assists to set up her teammates, making her one of the most valuable players in the game.

Caroline Graham Hansen
Club: Barcelona

Country: Norway

With 17 goals and 16 assists in 45 games, Graham Hansen was as prominent as ever during Barcelona's quadruple-winning season.

Alex Greenwood
Club: Manchester City

Country: England

The England defender captained Manchester City to domestic a domestic double, ending Chelsea's supremacy over the Women's Super League as well as securing another FA Cup title in a comprehensive 4-0 win over Brighton at Wembley.

Patri Guijarro
Club: Barcelona

Country: Spain

Guijarro played a vital role in Barcelona's engine room, ensuring the juggernauts stayed on top. Amid injuries and changes, the Spain midfielder's skill did not waver, making her one of the best players in the world.

Pernille Harder
Club: Bayern Munich

Country: Denmark

A prolific scorer, Harder's 35 goals and 12 assists made sure Bayern's domestic treble dreams stayed intact. She has won a domestic title every year since 2016 despite playing for three clubs in three different countries; 2025-26 was no different.

Yui Hasegawa
Club: Manchester City

Country: Japan

As one of the most underrated players, Hasegawa has flown under the radar, yet the Japan international started 20 WSL matches for City last season and maintained the English champions' standard to claim a second domestic title. She won her 100th cap for Japan during the country's title-winning Women's Asia Cup run.

Rose Lavelle
Club: Gotham FC

Country: United States

Lavelle was a crucial figure in securing Gotham's NWSL Challenge Cup with 14 goals and five assists in 40 games.

Mapi León
Club: Barcelona / London City Lionesses

Country: Spain

León was one of Barcelona's longest-serving players and started in 10 of the club's 11 Women's Champions League games on their way to lifting the trophy for the fourth time. This summer, though, she moved to emerging WSL team London City Lionesses.

Lorena
Club: Kansas City Current

Country: Brazil

The first-choice goalkeeper for both Kansas City Current and Brazil, she is of the most established goalkeepers in South American women's soccer. She is also nominated for the Women's Goalkeeper of the Year award.

Melvine Malard
Club: Manchester United / Chelsea

Country: France

Malard was one of Manchester United's standout players as they reached the Women's Champions League quarterfinals in what was the club's debut in the competition, notching four goals and four assists over the course of eight appearances. This summer, she made a blockbuster move to Chelsea.

Manaka Matsukubo
Club: North Carolina Courage / Chelsea

Country: Japan

Named the NWSL's best midfielder in 2025, Matsukubo followed up with a superb start to the 2026 season with five goals and four assists in nine games before joining Chelsea in July. At international level, she won the Women's Asia Cup with Japan.

Vivianne Miedema
Club: Manchester City

Country: Netherlands

Manchester City ended their decade-long wait for the Women's Super League title, and they could scarcely have done it without Miedema. The skillful forward started all but three of their league games last season, scoring 10 goals.

Ewa Pajor
Club: Barcelona

Country: Poland

When Barcelona need goals, Pajor is the first name they call upon. She was the 2025-26 Women's Champions League top scorer with 11 goals in 10 appearances. She is among the favorites for the Ballon d'Or Féminin.

Clàudia Pina
Club: Barcelona

Country: Spain

As prolific as her teammate Pajor is, Pina strikes a close second. She scored 21 goals in 27 games in Liga F last season, ending as the competition's top scorer.

Alexia Putellas
Club: Barcelona / London City Lionesses

Country: Spain

A favorite to win her third Ballon d'Or Féminin award, Putellas returned to being Barcelona's most crucial player in another landmark year, captaining the club to yet another quadruple. However, this summer, she ended her 12-year stay at the Camp Nou to join the London City Lionesses.

Wendie Renard
Club: OL Lyonnes

Country: France

Even at 36 years old, Renard is still among the gold standard of center backs in the game. She was one win away from extending her record of eight Women's Champions League titles, only to see defeat to Barcelona in the final.

Alessia Russo
Club: Arsenal

Country: England

With 18 goal contributions in 22 WSL games last season, Russo remains one of the best attacking threats in world soccer. She is also just one of two England players to make the short list alongside Manchester City's Alex Greenwood.

Khadija "Bunny" Shaw
Club: Manchester City

Country: Jamaica

With Manchester City not in European football last season, Shaw got to work focusing on scoring in the WSL and did so superbly. She finished as the competition's top scorer with 21 goals.

Momoko Tanikawa
Club: Bayern Munich

Country: Japan

Still only 21 years old, Tanikawa was an influential presence in the Bayern Munich midfield that helped the club reach the Women's Champions League semifinals, only to succumb to a hard-fought defeat to eventual champions Barcelona. At international level, she won the Women's Asia Cup with Japan.

Caroline Weir
Club: Real Madrid / OL Lyonnes

Country: Scotland

Last year, Weir became the first Scottish player to be nominated for the Ballon d'Or Féminin, and she follows up with another short list this time out. She netted 14 goals for Real Madrid in Liga F last season, as well as appearing in the Women's Champions League. In June, she moved to OL Lyonnes.

Tessa Wullaert
Club: Inter Milan

Country: Belgium

In her second season in Italy, Wullaert excelled with Inter Milan, scoring a league-high 14 goals, albeit the club did not manage to beat AS Roma to the Women's Serie A title.

Other awards and nominees

The crowning of European soccer's best men's and women's players are far from the only awards that France Football Magazine will hand out on the night. As ever, there will be prizes for the best clubs and coaches, as well as awards for the best U21 player, best goalkeeper, top scorer and the player who made outstanding humanitarian and social contributions.

stories.headline: Potential WNBA commissioner candidates to succeed Cathy Engelbert
stories.summary: Executives from the WNBA, NBA and Nike are among potential candidates to succeed Cathy Engelbert when she retires.
stories.body:
The WNBA is in search of a new leader, as commissioner Cathy Engelbert announced Friday that she will retire at the end of the calendar year.

Engelbert is the sixth league head and second-longest tenured behind Val Ackerman. Engelbert is the first to hold the title of WNBA commissioner, as the previous leaders served as president.

The process to find Engelbert's replacement will start later this month, if not sooner, sources told ESPN. Presumably, the hire will be made by and report to NBA commissioner Adam Silver, as was the case with Engelbert. She told the Associated Press and The IX that she has been working on a succession plan for years, and that she has already submitted a list of potential internal and external candidates to Silver.

It is unclear who else might have input on the decision, though the Board of Governors is expected to be involved. Prior to hiring Engelbert in 2019, the players' union also requested and was granted the opportunity to meet with the league's final candidates.

A source familiar with the situation told ESPN that the league is approaching the process with an open mind -- recognizing that the WNBA is now at a point where a leader without a traditional background in the corporate world might offer advantages.

Building and managing relationships with players, as well as owners, executives and business leaders, is also seen as a priority following Engelbert's tenure, which notably included several strained relationships with key players

Since Engelbert's announcement Friday, people around the league have speculated about who might be part of the candidate pool. Here are some of the names ESPN has heard as possibilities.

Swin Cash

The former UConn star played in the WNBA from 2002 to 2016, winning three championships. Inducted into the Naismith Hall of Fame in 2022, Cash has worked in the front office for the WNBA's New York Liberty (2017-19) and NBA's New Orleans Pelicans (2019-25). Cash, who turns 47 later this month, has also been a broadcast analyst. Her management experience is a plus, but some might question if Cash has spent enough time in the business world. -- Michael Voepel

Keia Clarke

She has been with the New York Liberty since 2011 and was promoted to CEO in 2020. She manages all business aspects of the franchise. Clarke played collegiate basketball at Canisius from 1999 to 2003 and began her career working for the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame. Clarke, 45, then went to work for the WNBA/NBA league offices before joining the Liberty. She has postgraduate business degrees from NYU and Harvard. Clarke knows the ins and outs of a WNBA franchise business and has been part of the huge growth of the Liberty in the past seven years. -- Voepel

Bethany Donaphin

Currently head of WNBA operations, Donaphin has been with the league since 2016. She played at Stanford from 1998 to 2002, then competed professionally in the WNBA and overseas from 2002 to 2008. She earned an MBA in 2012 from Pennsylvania's Wharton School and then spent 2013 to 2016 at Deloitte, consulting for Fortune 500 companies. Donaphin, 46, has worked with former WNBA president Lisa Borders and Engelbert at the WNBA. One of the questions regarding Donaphis is whether her close ties to Engelbert during the past seven years would be seen as a negative by the players, considering their criticisms of Engelbert. -- Voepel

Tanya Hvizdak

A vice president of global sports marketing at Nike, Hvizdak has spent 25 years at the company. Nike is the outfitter for the WNBA and NBA, agreeing to a 12-year extension for that role in 2024. Hvizdak has been closely involved in the development and rollout of shoes for prominent WNBA athletes such as A'ja Wilson, Caitlin Clark and Sabrina Ionescu. Hvizdak also spearheaded a Nike think tank, which included Serena Williams and Ionescu, in 2022 that focused on issues faced by female athletes. Hvizdak played collegiate basketball, first at Rhode Island and then Bentley, where she earned an MBA. Hvizdak has worked hard to elevate women's athletics and has extensive marketing and business knowledge. Would she want to relocate across the country from Portland to New York and take on a different type of role running the WNBA? -- Voepel

Nneka Ogwumike

If one of Engelbert's weaknesses was developing relationships with players, that's Ogwumike's clear strength. The Stanford grad is well-respected as WNBPA president for 10 years, a tenure that includes representing the players for two CBA negotiations. If Ogwumike is interested in the role, it would be a fascinating and unprecedented turn coming less than a year removed from a contentious labor negotiation between the players' union and the league/owners; Ogwumike has built a legacy representing the former, but the commissioner's job is to represent the latter.

Ogwumike, who recently announced she'll be retiring from the WNBA at the end of the season, has been asked if she would be interested in being WNBA commissioner. She responded, "I don't close doors, but I do appreciate vacation. There is so much that I don't know, and there is so much that I would have to learn before even, if an opportunity like that were to come for me, to be ready for that." So perhaps it's more realistic that Ogwumike would seek some other experiences first before pursuing that sort of leadership role. Either way, the league could gauge her interest in taking a sort of liaison role where she'd serve as a bridge between the league office and teams/players. -- Philippou

Jess Smith

In a similar vein to Clarke, Smith would be someone coming from the business side of a WNBA franchise. She has been at the helm as team president of the massively successful Golden State Valkyries since 2024. On the court, the Valkyries surpassed expectations by becoming the league's first expansion team to make the playoffs in its inaugural season. According to CNBC, the Valkyries are the first women's sports team with a $1 billion valuation. Smith has two decades of experience in pro sports, with previous stops at the team level in the MLB, NHL, MLS and NWSL. -- Philippou

Mark Tatum

Tatum, who previously served as the league's interim president between Lisa Borders' and Engelbert's tenures, would be a surprise pick in some respects. The league has had only female leaders. And, as the longtime deputy commissioner and COO of the NBA, he would be seen as an extension of Silver, putting into question how much autonomy the WNBA really has as a separate entity from the NBA. But if Tatum is seriously considered, it might indicate Silver isn't interested in achieving that dynamic. -- Philippou

ESPN's Ramona Shelburne also contributed to this report.

stories.headline: AFL chairman discusses 'meaningful change' for fixture
stories.summary: AFL chairman Craig Drummond has admitted there will be "meaningful change" to the fixture when Tasmania enter the competition in 2028.
stories.body:
AFL chair Craig Drummond admits shortening games are on the agenda as the league weighs up how to fixture the season when Tasmania enter the competition in 2028.

With the Devils to become the league's 19th team, AFL hierarchy are trying to work out the best structure.

Speaking at the SportNXT conference in Melbourne on Tuesday, Drummond knew the AFL needed to be "more thoughtful" about the draw.

"We talk about whether we should have a shorter game," Drummond said in an interview with Eddie McGuire.

"If we want to have more games?

"Do we need to have more games?

"If we want to have more games, we probably need a shorter game.

"Most football people would say, players certainly, and the PA (players association) would say we're probably just about maxed out on the number of minutes that players are playing.

"We will need to think carefully because we can't have the current number of rounds of 23.

"We need to have either 24 or something different.

"It is likely we'll see - and we are talking to the clubs, some meaningful change in our scheduling in 2028."

AFL and clubs discussed the future fixture conundrum during the season, with radical options like a mid-season tournament and a group stage after the home-and-away season floated.

Drummond, who was not asked about his involvement in the Geelong concussion saga, did make reference to the Pullman Hotel scandal involving several Sydney players.

"If you don't want to adhere to those values and expectations, then there's other opportunities outside sport," Drummond said.

"But within sport, as within business, we have high standards, high expectations, high values and we expect people to behave."

Drummond also revealed users of the AFL's app will be required to log-in from next year, saying it will be a "different experience".

The move comes amid a push to attract bigger audiences, especially into India.

stories.headline: Charles Leclerc's advice for Max vs 100 drivers: Don't crash into Verstappen!
stories.summary: Max Verstappen is set to race 100 drivers in a unique go-karting challenge, and his fellow Formula 1 rivals have given their two pence on how they think the race will go down.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen is set to race 100 drivers in a unique go-karting challenge, and his fellow Formula 1 rivals have given their predictions on how they think the race will go down.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Verstappen know each other very well on the karting track from years of battles when they were younger where they constantly fought for race wins.

Verstappen is returning to his racing roots and will be trying to overtake as many drivers as possible from the very back of the grid at Silverstone.

Leclerc has warned competitors that it would be "tough" to race against one of the best drivers of this generation, but to remember that he will have nine more rounds of the F1 season in front of him.

"I mean 100 [drivers] is a lot," he said.

"Ok, that would be fun. That would be cool. Honestly, the only advice I'll give is maybe not to crash into Max, because he's got a season to finish.

"And for Max to be careful, because I don't know how professional those drivers are, but 100 drivers is quite a lot on a track, so I think it would be fun.

"But obviously when you're racing against one of the best drivers in the world, they'll probably have a tough time."

This is unlike anything Verstappen has done before, and it will be taking place on a custom-built karting track in Silverstone on Sept. 16, just a few days after the Spanish Grand Prix.

Asked what he was most looking forward to about the live event, Verstappen said: "Just seeing the carnage unfold in front of me."

- Max vs 100: Verstappen to race drivers in karting event - live on Disney+

- Spanish Grand Prix 2026: Race start time in Madrid, how to watch

- Ferrari's vintage disaster-class paves way for Antonelli to win Italian GP

Mercedes' George Russell had a slightly different approach to taking on the Red Bull driver and advised that the competitors might need to be more tactical in order to keep the racing star behind.

Verstappen is known for his aggressive driving style and fearless overtaking and has four consecutive world championship titles to his name in F1.

"If you go full four abreast around the whole track he might be quite difficult to protect, so maybe a couple of drivers work as a team to try and block him," Russell advised.

The Englishman then found out that content creators and athletes will be racing against Verstappen, rather than professional racing drivers.

"He will be achieving that," Russell said. "I did a team race with 160 of my team members last week, and we had some top drivers, but yeah I think he should probably comfortably doing that task."

Max vs 100 will be broadcast live on Disney+ on Sept. 16.

stories.headline: Arena for 76ers, Flyers to open in 2030, marks 'new era'
stories.summary: The 76ers and Flyers have unveiled renderings of their new fully privately funded arena in South Philadelphia, which is targeted to open before the WNBA season in 2030.
stories.body:
The 76ers and Flyers have unveiled renderings of their new arena on the former Spectrum site in South Philadelphia, which the organizations are calling the largest fully privately funded project in city history.

The arena is now targeted to open before the WNBA season in 2030, when Philadelphia's expansion team will begin play. The Sixers, owned by Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment (HBSE), come in as 50-50 partners with Comcast Spectacor in the new arena, after spending more than a decade as tenants.

"This is a new era for Philadelphia sports," Comcast chairman Brian Roberts said. "To build our future where Ed Snider and the Spectrum made history makes this project truly special. Working with HBSE, we are creating a world-class experience worthy of Philadelphia's incredible fans."

The Spectrum-inspired design includes more than a half-acre of outdoor gathering space, with fan plazas, food and beverage options and a large entrance staircase inspired by the steps at the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

"Philly fans deserve the best arena in the world, and we are excited to partner with Comcast to deliver just that," Sixers managing partner Josh Harris said. "This privately funded arena will be the home to moments and memories that define this city for generations."

Added NBA commissioner Adam Silver: "I'm thrilled to see the first renderings of what promises to be an extraordinary home for NBA and WNBA basketball as well as many other world-class events. Beyond the incredible experience the new arena will bring to fans, I commend HBSE and Comcast for such a significant economic investment in Philadelphia."

For the Flyers, the move brings the franchise back to the grounds where it began play in 1967 and won its only two Stanley Cups.

Since taking over as Flyers governor in 2023, Dan Hilferty has also overseen a restructuring of Philadelphia's front office and made returning the franchise to consistent Stanley Cup contention a priority.

"This new arena will be a state-of-the-art home worthy of the Flyers, their fans, and the entire city," NHL commissioner Gary Bettman said. "Comcast Spectacor and HBSE's commitment to this project reflects a shared belief in Philadelphia's future and a lasting investment in the city's economic vitality."

The organizations project the arena will create nearly 15,000 jobs and generate nearly $6 billion in economic activity over the next decade, along with hundreds of millions of dollars in new tax revenue benefiting the city and the School District of Philadelphia.

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: Griezmann catapults Orlando into the playoff picture
stories.summary: With eight goal contributions in eight games since joining the Lions, Antoine Griezmann has turned around Orlando's season. That and more in ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday, another weekend of action is in the books, and it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

While Nashville dropped points in a 0-0 draw against New York City on Friday, their biggest competitors for the Supporters' Shield slipped up, too. Both Vancouver and Miami failed to win, leaving Nashville with a 10-point lead atop the Shield race.

2. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 2

Despite taking an early lead, the Whitecaps quickly crumbled in a 3-1 home defeat against St. Louis. In what was, perhaps, their worst match of the season, Vancouver fell apart before halftime en route to losing to fellow contender out West for the second time in four games.

3. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 7

You couldn't have written a better script for St. Louis' Saturday night. Not only did new additions Rafael Navarro and Damion Downs make their debuts in the second half, but the visitors took the game to Vancouver and secured a 3-1 road victory. Doubt St. Louis' contender status at your own peril.

4. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 3

Miami's Achilles heel is widely known: they're a team that gets easily scrambled in their own third. With two sloppy fouls conceding two penalties to Atlanta, Saturday's 2-2 draw with the Five Stripes was the latest example of Inter Miami's defensive play letting them down.

5. LAFC
Previous ranking: 5

Despite holding a one-goal lead heading into the intermission, LAFC's second-half concession saw them earn just a point on the road against Salt Lake. An unwillingness -- or inability -- to keep the ball late in games continues to bite for the Black & Gold.

6. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 6

After their scheduled meeting with D.C. United was postponed due to inclement weather, Cincinnati will have extra time to bed in their defensive reinforcements. That 4-0 loss to Nashville last time out still stings.

7. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 4

The good news? Chicago bagged four goals on Saturday, including one from Robert Lewandowski as he continues to find his place in the attack. The bad news? Chicago conceded four in a 4-4 draw with Toronto. It's safe to say Chicago are missing rising star Mbekezeli Mbokazi in the backline.

8. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 9

Up against a fearsome Nashville team, New York City manager Pascal Jansen opted for a fairly conservative approach on Friday. Ceding most of the ball, the Pigeons did well to keep Nashville scoreless, but they failed to create much danger themselves in a 0-0 home draw.

9. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 8

Trailing by two goals at halftime, the Revs couldn't find a way to equalize against the Galaxy on their way to a 2-1 road defeat. While Carles Gil's penalty conversion got them on the board, questions remain about whether the options New England have placed around him will produce.

10. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 10

Despite having a man advantage for the final 20-plus minutes of the match, Houston had a hard time creating much of anything in their 0-0 road draw with Charlotte. While attacking questions remain for Ben Olsen's outfit, the Dynamo's string of shutdown defensive showings mark them as a team that must be taken seriously.

11. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 13

While Charlotte couldn't find a breakthrough during their 0-0 home draw with Houston, Allan Saint-Maximin looked like the best player on the field. Dean Smith's new left winger was at the center of nearly every threatening move and has the look of an MLS star.

12. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 12

Still winless in league play since May, RSL drew 2-2 with LAFC on Saturday. They created a slew of quality chances, but also proved too open in defensive transition as control and tactical balance still eludes them.

13. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 16

Antoine Griezmann continued his absolute tear with the lone goal in Orlando's 1-0 win over San Diego. Now with eight goal contributions in eight games since debuting for the Lions, Griezmann has quickly turned around Orlando's season: they're now above the playoff line in the East.

14. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 14

If there's a debate about MLS's best striker, Petar Musa is doing his best to end it. The Croatia international managed two goals, including the game winner, and an assist in Dallas' 4-3 win over Kansas City. While the home side's focus lacked, Musa's certainly didn't.

15. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 15

Since league play resumed after the World Cup, the Union are yet to lose. Saturday's 2-0 victory over Montréal lengthened that streak of results to eight games, with six of them going down as wins. With yet another goal from Cavan Sullivan, Philadelphia are flying.

16. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 15

Missing star midfielder Jeppe Tverskov due to a card suspension, San Diego's ball progression never turned into regular chances in a 1-0 road loss to Orlando. Without the Dane, the sophomore side simply can't carry the same threat going forward.

17. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 11

For a team that prides itself on effective defending, conceding three goals in the first half in a 5-4 loss to the Timbers was nowhere near good enough for Minnesota. Still, breakout striker Marcus Caldeira's brace could signal longer-term attacking improvement for a team fighting for a playoff spot.

18. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 20

The Galaxy marked Sergi Roberto's first MLS start with a 2-1 victory over New England. The former Barcelona man was a touch magnet in central midfield, helping his new team conduct play. If Roberto and Chucky Lozano, who notched an assist, maintain this form, the Galaxy won't be easily dismissed.

19. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 22

Josh Sargent appears to be finding his form in MLS. While the U.S. striker had a quiet start to life in Toronto, he notched a hat trick in a 4-4 draw with Chicago over the weekend. It was a top-tier showing from Sargent atop Robin Fraser's attacking structure that led to a point for the hosts.

20. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 19

Now below the playoff line out East following a 0-0 draw in Seattle, that Red Bull New York didn't do more in the summer transfer window is a major concern. Without any game-changing additions made to the squad before deadline day, it's difficult to see how Michael Bradley's team will rebound.

21. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 21

On Saturday, Sounders fans could breathe a collective sigh of relief upon seeing Cristian Roldan make his first start for the team since May. Still, the USMNT midfielder's return wasn't enough to see Seattle claim their first win in months. A 0-0 draw with the Red Bulls had to suffice.

22. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 23

With star striker Kevin Kelsy now off to Rangers in the Scottish Premiership, replacement Vincent Janssen didn't waste any time filling the Venezuelan's shoes. Janssen notched a hat trick in the Timbers' wild 5-4 home win over Minnesota.

23. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 18

It looked as if the Quakes' winless run, one that stretches all the way back to May, was going to come to an end on Saturday. That is, until Austin managed a 97th-minute equalizer and a victory turned into a 1-1 draw for San Jose. The Earthquakes are in a bad, bad place.

24. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 24

D.C.'s meeting with Cincinnati was postponed due to weather, leaving the club without a chance to break a five-game winless streak.

25. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 25

Thanks to an equalizer from Guilherme Biro deep in second-half stoppage time, Austin secured a 1-1 draw against San Jose. The result marked four straight games without a loss in league play for the Texas capital club.

26. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 27

It didn't take Santi Rodriguez long to open his account in Columbus. The former New York City star bagged the opening goal for the Crew in a 3-0 victory over Colorado. With a remade attack, could this team make a late push for a spot in the postseason?

27. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 26

After trading Navarro to St. Louis and adding new pieces to the attack just before deadline day, the Rapids were nowhere near full strength in a 3-0 loss to the Crew. Colorado will have to wait for their new pieces to arrive and integrate to reach their full potential.

28. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 28

At last, there are signs of life in Atlanta. During their 2-2 draw with Miami, new striker Breel Embolo made his debut and scored a late equalizer from the spot. Elsewhere, young defensive midfielder Mauricio Amaro made his first MLS appearance and looked extremely comfortable amid his new surroundings.

29. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 29

Back to the bottom of the East after falling 2-0 in Philadelphia, it's difficult to see Montréal climbing the standings anytime soon. Even with Alexis Sánchez in the lineup, this team is still light on talent.

30. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 30

Although they managed one of their best attacking outings of the year, spurred on by new winger André Luiz's first start, Kansas City couldn't hold on for a point in Dallas. They fell 4-3 thanks to a late penalty by Musa.

stories.headline: Money isn't everything: Penrith star's big future hint
stories.summary: Penrith star Liam Martin has revealed he could forego more money elsewhere to stay at the Panthers, as he weighs up his future beyond the end of 2027.
stories.body:
Liam Martin has given the first real indication he could refuse more money elsewhere to stay at Penrith, declaring the dollar-figure on his NRL contract won't be the only deciding factor in his future.

Martin has put contract talks with the Panthers on hold until after the end of the season, with the focus now clearly on Sunday's qualifying final against Sydney Roosters.

The Panthers have a number of stars off contract at the end of next season, with Nathan Cleary and Isaah Yeo's future also yet to be locked in beyond 2027.

Moses Leota is another star off contract, with the prop forward also indicating on Tuesday he would find it hard to leave the foot of the mountains.

But the sheer number of big names off contract has left Penrith in a difficult position, juggling several offers under the salary while trying to retain all talent.

If Martin remains unsigned by November 1, the Kangaroos Test forward would likely command more money on the open market.

The tax-free money from PNG would also loom as an option, given the NRL has not allowed the Chiefs to sign Hudson Young for their initial offer of $900,000 a season after Canberra offered him $1.1 million to stay.

But Martin made clear money would not be the only thing he would consider, and there was a real appeal to staying at Penrith.

"There could be more money elsewhere, but money is not everything at the end of the day," Martin said.

"I have a great bunch of mates here, best mates who I have been with since I was 18.

"I have been in Penrith for 10 years now and have a little boy. There is a lot to weigh up, it's not an easy decision. It's one I'll have to make in due time."

Since Penrith's run began in 2021, they have lost more than half of their first title-winning team to rival clubs.

Until this point none of Penrith's home-grown talent have lined up against them in a grand final, with the likes of Apisai Koroisau and Jarome Luai yet to play finals at Wests Tigers.

"There's a duality to it," Martin said.

"I couldn't imagine going somewhere and experiencing failure and just how tough it would be.

"But also the challenge of building a successful club somewhere else, I feel like I could offer something. It's a tough decision.

"That success is so addictive, and what we've got here is an incredible culture."

Penrith have already lost Brian To'o to the Chiefs for 2028, while Yeo is edging closer to formalising a new deal.

The Panthers also remain confident they can keep Cleary, who has not put a timeline on his decision.

Leota, meanwhile, is expected to stay, but said he was unsure if a deal would be done by November 1.

"Penrith is my home and this is all I have ever known," Leota said on Tuesday.

"It would be hard to get me away from here, but we'll see what happens."
